summary: Verified Database Abstraction Layer end-to-end. MongoDB mode regression PASS (15/15 pytest). Flipped DB_TYPE=couchbase and ran read-only smoke: 14/14 pytest PASS, counts match exactly (47 users, 8 buildings, 17 floors, 160 slots, 74 reservations). New GET /api/system/db-info returns correct payload with proper 401/403 auth guards. Frontend DbStatusBadge renders green MONGODB and red COUCHBASE CAPELLA in admin sidebar; not shown to non-admins. DB_TYPE restored to 'mongodb'.

minor.issue: Returns 403 when no auth cookie present rather than 401. Still acceptable - test accepts either - but a stricter 401 for truly anonymous requests is conventional.

couchbase_mode.pytest_passed: 14/14 (write test deliberately skipped per review note)

verification_matrix.badge_admin_only: Non-admin user session does NOT render the sidebar badge (admin layout not reached by non-admin; confirmed).

critical_code_review_comments: system.py host-parsing for Mongo splits on '@' and '/' which is OK for basic mongodb:// URIs but could expose query params for SRV/replicaset URIs. Acceptable for now since MONGO_URL here is localhost-only.
DbStatusBadge silently hides on error (if !info) - that's fine UX, but consider logging for admins.
init_db/close_db exist but server.py appears to rely on Motor's lazy-eager connect. Verify close_db() is wired to FastAPI shutdown for clean connection teardown (esp. Couchbase).
auth guard returns 403 (require_admin) instead of 401 for unauthenticated requests. Not blocking but 401 is conventional when credentials are missing.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (badge renders correctly in both modes; admin-only)

seed_data_creation: None. Test created and cleaned up a single TEST_abstraction_user@example.com during MongoDB CRUD test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: DB_TYPE is restored to 'mongodb' in /app/backend/.env. The test file /app/backend/tests/test_db_abstraction.py is safe to run in either mode (CRUD test auto-skips when DB is not MongoDB). Couchbase cluster egress IP 34.170.12.145 is allowlisted; Couchbase init takes ~15-25s on backend restart due to index warm-up. Do NOT run destructive mutations against Couchbase - the bucket holds the migrated ~815-doc dataset.
